decisions: User: final Stability, Performance and Security phases certify the exact hosted draft binaries that get published.
User: only a recovery-mode restore may create a database key while an unreadable primary exists; every other existing-data path fails closed.
Immutable releases stay off until the user decides the trade-off with automatic re-draft containment.
changes: Publish containment: step caps and budget lint, retried re-draft, exec'd publisher with SIGINT/SIGTERM re-draft, async attestation calls, in-flight publish settling and draft confirmation.

Draft mutations by release id through draft-assets.mjs with id-scoped uploads; per-asset digest confirmation; runtime gh flag probe; shared release notes, workflow parser and strict JSON owners; Vale drift warning.

Key storage: one process-wide vault key with single-flight native loads, re-read before any key creation, passphrase changes under the cache lock, and no database key creation while backups, restore or update-snapshot artifacts exist.
Recovery screen warns that a recovery restore can create a key that makes earlier data unreadable; restore status copy is accurate; dropped backups are refused during startup recovery.
